extractor_notes: 1) The description gives exactly one event, so there is one observation. The event list carries explicit negative statements ('No sexual activity is shown and no nudity is visible'); these are recorded as descriptors on o1 rather than as separate observations, because no nudity event occurred to observe. 2) o1 is_depicted is false: what is shown is the aftermath, and the sex itself is established only through dialogue. The scene itself is on screen, so this is the distinction the field asks about and not an omission. 3) treatment is 'fictional' because the asset is a scripted sitcom episode; the description does not say the scene is played for laughs, so 'comedic' is not recorded even though the genre line says 'sitcom'. Genre is not scene framing. 4) Two transmissions are recorded. The description names a +1 timeshift channel on the same service, so the same file goes out twice; t2's 15:30 start is derived from the meaning of '+1' and is flagged in not_stated. 5) 'timecode_clock' is 'elapsed' because 00:11:40 falls inside the stated 22-minute runtime; the source does not say which clock it uses. 6) is_news_or_current_affairs is set to 'no' on the strength of the stated 'sitcom' content type, which is a direct statement that the asset is scripted comedy, not a genre inference about audience. 7) is_made_primarily_for_children is left not_stated: a general entertainment sitcom is not stated to be a children's programme and the description does not say. 8) No access control is mentioned anywhere, which is itself recorded in not_stated because the service is pay TV and a gate would change the slot analysis.
